_comment: SYNTHETIC discharge protocols served by the MCP resource discharge://protocol/{condition}. Generated for this capstone. Simplified for demonstration and NOT a clinical reference.

heart-failure.title: Discharge protocol — Acute decompensated heart failure
required_before_discharge: Patient at or near documented dry weight for at least 24 hours
Oral diuretic regimen established for a minimum of 24 hours before discharge
Basic metabolic panel within 24 hours of discharge, with potassium and creatinine stable
Guideline-directed medical therapy reviewed and uptitrated where blood pressure and renal function allow
Patient or caregiver able to demonstrate daily weight monitoring

follow_up.primary: Cardiology or heart-failure clinic within 7 days of discharge
follow_up.high_risk: Within 3-5 days, plus a telephone check at 48-72 hours
follow_up.labs: Basic metabolic panel within 5-7 days of any diuretic or RAAS-agent change

education_priorities: Weigh at the same time each morning and record it
Report a gain of more than 2 kg (about 4 lb) in 2 days or 2.5 kg in a week
Limit sodium to under 2 grams per day
Never stop a heart medication without speaking to the clinic first
red_flags: Weight gain of more than 2 kg in 2 days
Breathlessness at rest or needing extra pillows to sleep
New or worsening swelling of the ankles or abdomen
Light-headedness, fainting, or a heart rate under 50
heart-failure.readmission_risk_note: Heart failure carries one of the highest 30-day readmission rates. Early follow-up and reliable weight monitoring are the two interventions with the strongest effect.

copd.title: Discharge protocol — COPD exacerbation
required_before_discharge: Stable on the intended home oxygen regimen for at least 24 hours
Inhaler technique observed and corrected
Course of steroids and antibiotics defined with an explicit end date
Smoking-cessation support offered where relevant

follow_up.primary: Primary care or respiratory clinic within 7-14 days
follow_up.high_risk: Within 7 days, with pulmonary rehabilitation referral

education_priorities: Use the rescue inhaler correctly and know when to escalate
Complete the full steroid and antibiotic course
Recognise an exacerbation early and start the action plan
red_flags: Breathlessness that does not improve with the rescue inhaler
Blue tinge to the lips or fingertips
copd.readmission_risk_note: Pulmonary rehabilitation referral within 30 days measurably reduces readmission.

pneumonia.title: Discharge protocol — Community-acquired pneumonia
required_before_discharge: Afebrile for at least 24 hours
Oxygen saturation at or above 92 percent on room air at rest and on ambulation
Tolerating oral intake and oral antibiotics
Antibiotic course defined with an explicit end date

follow_up.high_risk: Within 7 days for patients over 65 or with comorbidity
follow_up.labs: Follow-up chest radiograph at 6 weeks to confirm radiographic resolution

education_priorities: Complete the entire antibiotic course even once feeling well
Expect fatigue and cough to persist for several weeks
Return if symptoms worsen after initial improvement
red_flags: Fever returning after it had settled
Confusion, especially in an older patient
pneumonia.readmission_risk_note: Confirm radiographic resolution at 6 weeks; a persistent opacity warrants further investigation.

dvt-pe.title: Discharge protocol — Venous thromboembolism (DVT / PE)
required_before_discharge: Anticoagulation regimen defined with an explicit intended duration
For warfarin: INR trending into range and a documented anticoagulation-clinic appointment
Bleeding-risk counselling completed and documented
Interacting medications reviewed against the anticoagulant

follow_up.high_risk: INR within 3 days where an interacting medication has been started
follow_up.labs: INR per anticoagulation-clinic schedule; full blood count at 2 weeks

education_priorities: Take the anticoagulant at the same time every day and never double a missed dose
Recognise bleeding that needs urgent attention
Tell every clinician and dentist about the anticoagulant
Keep vitamin K intake steady if taking warfarin
red_flags: Bleeding that will not stop, or blood in the urine or stool
A severe headache or any head injury
dvt-pe.readmission_risk_note: Warfarin interactions are the dominant cause of early readmission in this group. Any new interacting medication requires an INR check within 3 days.

post-surgical.title: Discharge protocol — General post-surgical
required_before_discharge: Pain controlled on oral analgesia
Tolerating diet and passing urine independently
Wound reviewed and care instructions given
Mobilising at or near baseline, or with an equipment plan in place

follow_up.high_risk: Wound review within 7 days where infection risk is elevated

education_priorities: Keep the wound clean and dry; know what normal healing looks like
Follow the lifting and activity restrictions
Take analgesia proactively rather than waiting for severe pain
red_flags: Spreading redness, warmth or discharge from the wound
post-surgical.readmission_risk_note: Surgical-site infection is the leading cause of readmission; early wound review matters most in the first week.

diabetes.title: Discharge protocol — Diabetes-related admission
required_before_discharge: Stable glucose on the intended home regimen for 24 hours
Insulin or oral agent technique demonstrated
Hypoglycaemia recognition and treatment taught
Glucose monitoring supplies confirmed available at home

follow_up.primary: Primary care or endocrinology within 7-14 days
follow_up.high_risk: Within 7 days after any insulin regimen change
follow_up.labs: HbA1c if not measured within 3 months; renal function if agents were changed

education_priorities: Check glucose as instructed and record the readings
Recognise and treat a low glucose promptly
Follow sick-day rules for medication adjustment
red_flags: Vomiting and unable to keep fluids down
A low glucose that does not respond to sugar
diabetes.readmission_risk_note: Reliable access to monitoring supplies and medication at home is the single strongest predictor of early readmission in this group.
